item: Democrats won the Texas governorship; Abbott had paused new rural AI data centres. Texas was due to host about a quarter of new US data-centre capacity by 2030.
note: Inference: power/permitting risk for grid-dependent leveraged builders; raises the value of on-site power (gas turbines, microreactors).

item: US midterms: Democrats won House (~255) and Senate (~55). Nasdaq-100 futures -2%, Nikkei ~-4% on the night.
A Democratic Senate makes extension of expiring OBBB tax cuts (from late 2028) less likely.

NVIDIA reportedly told data-centre partners (verbally) that at least 51% of revenue must come from non-China clients; also reports about Jensen Huang's ties to a person linked to Chinese intelligence.
Saudi Aramco Q3 profit +35% on high oil prices while Saudi GDP shrank 3.8%; plot against Syria's Homs refinery foiled.
US ammonia imports from Trinidad down 34%, adding to fertiliser inflation.
Trump says $4bn/yr military aid to Israel will wind down by year-end, earlier than the 2028 expiry.
Iran's energy-squeeze strategy: US gasoline above $4, diesel above $6. Democrats can cut Pentagon funding to pressure an end to the Iran war.
note: Bears on H2 kill signal K2 (Hormuz/Iran deal collapsing diesel prices).

item: Trump 2.0 pivoting to stabilise US-China ties: trade-truce renewals, flexibility on chip controls, 'transactional' noises on Taiwan.
Trump may push Ukraine toward land-for-peace; possible Xi/Putin meetings at APEC; US pushing Europe to fund US arms for Ukraine (PURL).
note: Inference: tilts defense spending toward Europe/NATO.

item: Indonesia: Prabowo deployed 20,000+ troops to Jakarta after arresting aides; 'market jitters'.
US claimed strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz; Vance says a deal 'could be close'; US fuel prices at records.
Hackers sabotaged supermarket refrigeration in six European countries; Russia suspected, possibly testing NATO Article 5.
Belgium near government collapse over an $11bn budget gap; debt >108% of GDP; borrowing costs at 15-year highs.
GMO Internet Group (9449.T) ransomware hit its cloud/forex platform; its 2031 bond spreads widened 50bp.
Direct Ukraine-Russia talks confirmed for Abu Dhabi next week; Trump may want a deal at APEC or G20.
ISW: Russia lost net territory in Ukraine for a second month; Ukraine claims a record 54,000 Russian casualties.
Xi's purges leave the Central Military Commission with two members; 71 senior officials under investigation in nine months; fourth term expected at the 2027 Party Congress.
Turkey detained 85 members of a network linked to Russian arson at a Starlink ground station in Poland.
Speculation Netanyahu (caretaker PM) could join US in resuming strikes on Iran; Cambodia cruise costs jumped after Hormuz squeeze.
Houthis claimed another hit on Saudi Ras Tanura refinery; crude +1.62%.
Woodside selling its 33% Greater Sunrise gas stake to Timor-Leste's state firm.

Indonesia: Prabowo deployed 20,000 troops to Jakarta after investigators say his chief of staff (ex-police chief Listyo) ran unauthorised surveillance on him. The rupiah is at record lows, the central bank governor quit early in July, and MSCI has threatened a downgrade over the opaque equity market.
note: Inference: rising EM/SE Asia risk premium; the Iran-war energy shock is hitting importers.

item: Trump after hosting Putin's envoy: a 'big agreement' coming that 'might involve all of Europe'; Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi next week.
note: Inference: a ceasefire would change the defense-tech demand story (Anduril, GA, drones).

item: 21+ flights across Europe got fake bomb threats on Thursday, the third day of hoaxes this week.
Leaked documents show Russia plans to supply Iran with 90 helicopter-mounted LMUR missile launchers.
note: Inference: points to a longer Iran war, so oil and diesel stay high; works against H2's Hormuz/Iran-deal kill signal.

item: South Korea is expanding naval operations toward Hormuz and Somalia (anti-piracy, mine clearing). The Iran war has drained Western naval capacity and Somali piracy is filling the gap; Korea imports nearly all its oil.

France: 600k-1.5m on strike over wages and the cost of living, six months before elections Le Pen is forecast to win; Paris must choose between concessions that worsen its fiscal crisis and growing protests.
note: Inference: adds to European sovereign stress (with Belgium, Nov 3).

item: Paraguay: President Peña resigned after the collapse of digital bank Ueno (about 10% of the state pension fund's portfolio); he had resisted pressure to drop recognition of Taiwan.
note: Inference: small risk to one of Taiwan's few diplomatic allies.

item: Jensen Huang apologised for an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a Singapore-based exec US intelligence says works for China's MSS. She worked for Megaspeed, which bought $4.8bn of advanced chips via Southeast Asian affiliates and which US officials call an MSS front. Nvidia's board says there's no reason to believe secrets were compromised and has opened an independent investigation; Trump called Huang 'an honourable guy'.
note: Data: NVDA pre-market $177.75 on 2026-11-09, -4.8% vs the $186.64 close (yfinance). Inference: key-person and governance risk at the compute leader.

item: The newsletter expects Washington hawks to push for tighter chip controls: closing the Southeast Asia re-export loophole and treating key AI firms more like defense contractors (counter-intel briefings, disclosure rules). A short-seller flagged the ties in May.
note: Inference: reverses the easing trend noted Nov 5; China is Nvidia's second-largest market.

item: After the midterm loss Trump replaced chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller.
note: Inference: less bipartisan compromise ahead of two years of House oversight; more domestic, less deal-making abroad.

item: China and Gabon elevated ties, signing pacts on security, trade and mining that secure priority access to Gabon's manganese (an EV battery input).
The lead piece also cites Elon Musk's Starlink throttling and Anthropic's collapsed Pentagon negotiations as examples of tech leaders holding outsized geopolitical power.

Jensen Huang and Nvidia face a shareholder class action alleging they concealed his ties to Megaspeed, the Singapore firm alleged to have smuggled chips to China; reports also claim Nvidia may have intervened in a US probe of Megaspeed (Reuters, 2026-11-09).
note: Data: NVDA closed $178.67 on 2026-11-09, -4.3% vs $186.64 on Nov 6 and -10.7% vs $200.13 on Nov 4 (yfinance). Inference: litigation adds to key-person risk ahead of Nov 17 earnings.

item: Trump said the military part of the Iran war is 'effectively over' after meeting Qatar's PM; Rubio says no breakthrough is near. Brent fell 1.7% to $90.99 per the newsletter.
note: Data: Brent futures $91.31 on 2026-11-10 vs $98.32 on Nov 6, about -7% (yfinance BZ=F). Relevant to H2.K2 (Hormuz reopening / Iran deal collapses diesel and inflation expectations).

item: ECB President Lagarde leaves in Feb 2027, early, to lock in technocratic leadership before 2027 elections. Two-man race: Klaas Knot (slightly more hawkish, economists' frontrunner) and Pablo Hernandez de Cos (BIS). EU leaders aim to decide by Christmas.
note: Inference: Le Pen, now favourite for France, has called on the ECB to buy French debt; a euro-sceptic win would pressure EU bond markets and add to global long-end yield stress.

item: ExxonMobil signed a preliminary deal with Venezuela's interim government to explore drilling, months after calling the country 'uninvestable'.
GAO: about 17,000 F-35 parts worth ~$1.3bn are missing from the Pentagon's logistics database.
US, Russian and Ukrainian delegates resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi; reports say Washington asked whether Russia would accept a NATO-like Western guarantee for Ukraine.
France blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for last month's cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration systems and issued arrest warrants for the Shahid Kaveh cyber unit.

Deep dive on Alice Huang and Megaspeed: an obscure gaming subsidiary (7Road International) rebranded as Megaspeed, got 'Nvidia Cloud Partner' status within months and bought $5-7bn (140-240k) of restricted H100/H200 chips. Commerce found ~50,000 chips unaccounted for. Ownership moved to Swiftdata, a new Singapore entity, letting Nvidia tell Washington there was no Chinese equity. Singapore confirms it is investigating Megaspeed. Huang has vanished.
note: Data: NVDA closed $168.89 on 2026-11-10, -5.5% on the day and -15.6% vs $200.13 on Nov 4 (yfinance). Inference: the questions now reach Nvidia's own partner vetting, not just Huang's private life.

item: Singapore filings suggest Alibaba was Megaspeed's lead financier and anchor client; chips were routed via server farms used by Chinese tech giants including Alibaba.
note: Data: BABA closed $102.72 on 2026-11-10 vs $109.45 on Nov 6, -6.1% (yfinance). Alibaba is not in the tracker universe.

item: China's trade surplus passed $1T in the first ten months of 2026, on track to beat the 2025 full-year record of $1.2T (CNBC).
note: Inference: supports more tariff and export-control pressure from trading partners.

item: World Bank projects an 800m job shortfall in developing countries over 15 years: 1.2bn young people entering, ~400m jobs on track.
House Republicans blocked Massie's impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Hegseth (abuse of power, unauthorised Iran war).
Abu Dhabi US-Russia-Ukraine talks: Zelensky calls day one 'constructive'; the newsletter expects at most a prisoner swap.
Syria weighs sending special forces to help Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, after a $400m Saudi loan.
XPeng two-seat flying cars could launch in China as soon as next summer (Guardian).

item: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA president, CEO and director, effective Nov 11. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO (and stays CFO) while the board searches; Harvey C. Jones (director since 1993) becomes chair. Source: NVIDIA 8-K Item 5.02 filed 2026-11-12 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000082/nvda-20261111.htm). Reuters also reports a relationship with a second employee.
note: Data: NVDA closed $166.19 on 2026-11-12, -4.3% on the day and -17.0% vs $200.13 on Nov 4 (yfinance). Inference: founder-CEO exit at the compute leader five days before Nov 17 earnings; first test of whether the AI trade was priced partly on Huang himself.

item: Treasury Secretary Bessent called on Nvidia to pick an outside CEO and gave it 10 days to answer questions on internal culture, export-control compliance and whether it ignored shell-company red flags. Some employees and Silicon Valley figures are campaigning to reinstate Huang, who has reportedly discussed a return with allies (Bloomberg). Interim CEO Kress presents Q3 results Tue Nov 17.
note: Data: NVDA closed $156.14 on 2026-11-16, -22.0% vs $200.13 on Nov 4 (yfinance). Inference: the government is now a party to the CEO choice; earnings call is the first read on whether China-linked demand guidance changes.

item: US negotiators floated Ukraine ceding all of Donbas in exchange for NATO membership (first time raised, per Zelensky). Russia's opening paper asks NATO to pull back to 1997 borders; Trump says a deal 'will involve all of Europe'. EU named a negotiating team (UK, France, Germany, Italy, Poland). Large prisoner swap agreed.

Yemen's Saudi-backed forces retreated from the area overlooking the Bab al-Mandeb; Houthis within 60 km of Aden. IRGC drones targeted a US radar at Bahrain's Riffa Air Base (second strike in three days, intercepted).
note: Data: Brent $92.88 on 2026-11-17, up from $91.31 on Nov 10 (yfinance BZ=F).

item: More than 18,000 US flights cancelled since Friday after a communications outage forced a four-hour nationwide ground stop, the longest since 9/11.

Australia and the Philippines signed a Defence Cooperation Agreement at the ASEAN summit (maritime surveillance and drones). Estonia will close its Russian border from Dec 1 after an alleged sabotage attempt against drone maker Threod Systems.

Commerce added Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil to its list of countries with an 'unacceptable risk of diversion' for advanced AI chips, targeting the data-centre loophole by which Chinese users rent top chips abroad (Al Jazeera). Brazil follows big ByteDance, Alibaba and Huawei data-centre plans there.
note: Data: Nov 16 closes - NVDA $156.14 (-4.1% d/d), TSM $373.45 (-6.3%), AVGO $333.40 (-3.9%) (yfinance). Inference: Southeast Asian AI data-centre projects, including Thailand's, now face licence friction; demand that routed through them shifts or stalls.

item: Lead story: Houthis now dominate the Bab al-Mandeb (~10% of global maritime trade) after taking Mocha and Perim; government forces retreated toward Aden, Taiz is encircled. A Houthi embargo is crippling Saudi energy exports. The Saudis fired their coalition commander.
note: Inference: keeps a risk premium in oil and shipping even as the Iran war winds down, working against H2.K2 (diesel and breakevens falling).

item: APEC leaders gather in Shenzhen; Trump becomes the first US president to visit. The newsletter expects the US-China trade truce to roll over. Trump's first Quad meeting was scheduled for 55 minutes.
Ukraine collapsed a segment of the Kerch Bridge, blocking the shipping channel; the EU passed more Russia sanctions. Russian aircraft entered Japanese airspace.

Nvidia's board used the Q3 call to reject a Musk-backed petition to reinstate Jensen Huang. Q3 FY27 (8-K/EX-99.1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000088/q3fy27pr.htm): revenue $115.8bn (+20% q/q, +103% y/y); Data Center $107.6bn (+110% y/y); GAAP GM 74.8%; GAAP EPS $2.70. Q4 guide $130.0bn +/-3% (includes an extra week), assumes no China Data Center compute revenue, GM 71-72%. Vera Rubin NVL72 shipping, incl. at CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Azure, OCI, Nebius, coming to SpaceX. Returned $28.1bn in Q3; $227.3bn buyback authorisation left.
note: Data: NVDA closed $155.46 on Nov 17 (before results); pre-market $159.78 (+2.8%) on Nov 18 (yfinance). Inference: demand for compute is intact and the stock's fall has been about governance and policy, not orders. Neocloud customers (CRWV, NBIS) named as Rubin hosts.

item: Inside Deutsche Bank: a 50+ newsroom consortium published the largest banking leak (15m files): Russian oligarch clients (17 sanctioned-list clients = half of private Russian revenue by Nov 2020), payments tied to suspected North Korean fronts, a suspected Al Qaeda financier with 'no additional actions', $22bn/yr of Colombian euro flows with zero SARs, $600m suspicious Epstein transfers, and tax structures for Aldi and Siemens owners. DB says the issues are years old.
note: Data: DB (NYSE) closed $33.88 on Nov 17 vs $36.62 on Nov 13, -7.5% (yfinance). Not in the tracker universe. Inference: European bank regulatory and fine risk; a reminder of the newsletter's populism theme in Germany.

item: Xi and Putin said Moscow and Beijing should 'lead the trend towards a multipolar world' ahead of the Trump-Xi-Putin three-way at APEC Shenzhen.
Macron secured an exemption from Malaysia's raw rare-earth export ban as ties were upgraded; Malaysia is easing the ban selectively for partners who co-invest locally (France's Carester JV).

Mongolia's president will resign over alleged $25m kickbacks on the coking-coal railway to China. The World Bank is weighing a budget-support freeze on Somalia after its top court ruled the president's mandate expired.
IEA November Oil Market Report: supply rising, refinery runs falling, demand forecast to fall.
note: Inference: bearish oil backdrop supports H2.K2, offset by Red Sea risk.

item: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 (above the $70-78 range), Nasdaq ticker ANT, debut Nov 19. 424B4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2130357/000162828026074944/anthropicpbc-424b4.htm): 980.0m Class A shares (956.35m primary, 23.65m by sellers) = $81.3bn gross, the largest IPO on record (SpaceX raised $75bn). Concurrent $26.0bn private placement of Class N shares at the IPO price to Google (part of its 2026 investment commitment), Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA and TSMC Partners. Newsletter: ~7x oversubscribed, $1.5T valuation.
note: Valuation is the newsletter's figure, not checked. Inference: chip suppliers and a hyperscaler are buying equity in a compute customer; the same vendor-financing loop H1.C5 tracks with Broadcom. Anthropic makes the assistant that maintains this tracker.

item: The memory shortage ('Rammageddon') pushed Xbox into another console price rise; Microsoft warned 'we expect another doubling [of memory prices] by the fall of 2027'. US tariffs cut China's share of US-bound consoles from 86% to 5%; Vietnam is now #1.
note: Data: SK Hynix KRW 1,183,000 and Samsung KRW 196,900 on 2026-11-19; SNDK $776.22 on Nov 18 (yfinance). Inference: supports H1.T3 bottleneck revenue growth holding.

item: Follow-up to Q3: no new NVIDIA news in this issue.
note: Data: NVDA closed $150.96 on 2026-11-18, -2.9% the day after results that beat (yfinance).

item: Trump-Xi-Putin three-way summit under way in Shenzhen. Kerch Bridge hit a third time this week.
Hegseth signed a defence cooperation deal with Venezuela's interim leader Rodriguez. Seven EU members (led by France and Germany) want 'shield' dropped from the $26bn European Space Defence Shield.
note: The lead piece cites Anduril at a $61bn valuation (newsletter figure).

item: Thai PM Anutin used his APEC speech to back linking the ASEAN power grid to Japan's regional clean-energy initiative.
ICJ found Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya, the first time it has found a state responsible. About 413t of African gold (~$52bn) was smuggled to the UAE in 2024.
Taiwan's Taiex fell 6.2% on Friday Nov 20 and 18% on the week amid a wider Asian rout on AI-bubble worries; some investors ask whether Anthropic's record IPO marked the top (Bloomberg).
note: Data (yfinance): ^TWII 43,675 (Nov 13) -> 36,033 (Nov 20) = -17.5% week, -6.2% Fri. Nov 20 day moves: NVDA $125.53 (-14.0%), AVGO $304.41 (-12.2%), CRWV $39.51 (-12.0%), TSM $318.71 (-9.5%), 2330.TW TWD 2,000 (-4.8%), Samsung -7.0%, SK Hynix -5.9%, Tokyo Electron -7.1%. NVDA -37% vs $200.13 on Nov 4. Inference: the fall now hits bottleneck and leveraged names together, which is broad AI de-risking rather than the credit-first pattern H1 predicts.

item: Anthropic (ANT) debuted Nov 19 after the record $81.3bn IPO at $83.
note: Data: ANT closed $97.17 on Nov 19 (+17% vs IPO price) and $88.91 on Nov 20 (-8.5%) (yfinance).

item: A Houthi missile hit Riyadh's tallest tower, home of Saudi Arabia's ~$900bn PIF sovereign fund, a week after hitting the Aramco tower.
note: Data: Brent $92.57 on Nov 20 (yfinance BZ=F), little changed on the week.

item: APEC adopted the 'Shenzhen Outlook' (supply-chain resilience, paperless trade). The Trump-Xi-Putin huddle produced a joint 'peace declaration' against nuclear war and little else; Putin may attend Trump's G20 summit next month. The Quad held its first in-person Trump-era summit (maritime surveillance, undersea cables). ASEAN again failed to finish the South China Sea Code of Conduct.
A US consortium won the rights to develop Kenya's Mrima Hill rare-earth project (~$60bn of minerals); the Australian-led rival is challenging. Chinese miners won a separate copper project.

ICJ ruled 9-6 that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya (first ICJ finding of state genocide). Bukele seeks a third term. Spain holds a snap election Nov 29. South Korea's top court overturned ex-PM Han's 15-year sentence.

COP31 in Turkey collapsed on Nov 22 with no overarching deal, the first since 2009 by some definitions. Petrostates watered down any reference to fossil fuels and pushed carbon capture; adaptation fund pledges were just $50.2m; the Loss and Damage Fund holds $822m against $2.8bn of requests. No leader from China, the US or India attended.
note: Inference: no new global push on fossil-fuel phase-out; demand for firm low-carbon power (nuclear) rests on data-centre and military buyers, not climate diplomacy.

item: A Dutch court imposed a temporary EU sales ban on BYD's Ti7 hybrid SUV for being too similar to the Land Rover Defender; BYD shares fell ~2% on Monday.
note: Inference: minor competitive relief for Tesla in Europe.

item: A Ukrainian drone set ablaze a US-sanctioned Russian logistics ship in Finnish waters; another drone sank a Russian warship refuelling in Libya. Finland's PM warned the war is 'spilling over'.
note: Inference: Baltic shipping and insurance risk rising.

item: India's Congress youth wing protested at Meta's offices with a seven-day ultimatum to restore restricted Instagram accounts of opposition figures; India is Meta's biggest market by users.

UN Security Council's ninth straw poll for Secretary-General deadlocked; Guterres's term ends Dec 31. MBS reportedly ordered the arrest of NEOM's former head. Mexico captured cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro'.

NVIDIA's board reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO and director on Nov 22, effective immediately; Kress returns to CFO only (8-K Item 5.02, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000090/nvda-20261122.htm). The newsletter says this followed a personal intervention by Trump, who said there was 'no evidence' of unlawful conduct. The same day Washington blacklisted Megaspeed. Senator Cotton pledges an investigation and a tougher chip export-control bill; Democrats take Congress in January.
note: Data: NVDA closed $165.05 on 2026-11-23, +31.5% from $125.53 on Nov 20 (yfinance), the newsletter's 'largest single-day gain for any stock in US history' (~$1T). Still -17.5% vs $200.13 on Nov 4. Inference: the government now has visible leverage over NVIDIA; export-control risk shifts from the White House to Congress.

item: Market reaction to Huang's reinstatement.
note: Data (yfinance): Nov 23 TSM $363.60 (+14.1%), CRWV $48.33 (+22.3%), AVGO $313.55 (+3.0%); Nov 24 Taiex 40,122 (+9.0%), SK Hynix KRW 1,158,000 (+6.7%). ANT $87.64 (-1.4%). Inference: last week's 'AI bubble' rout reversed in one day on a single personnel decision, a sign the sell-off was sentiment and positioning, and that the group trades as one block on NVIDIA headlines.

item: Washington blacklisted Megaspeed (the Singapore firm alleged to have routed Nvidia chips to China); NYT reports Alice Huang liaised directly with an MSS officer for more than a year.

Australia is offering the Solomon Islands $667m under a security treaty to be signed Nov 25, replacing China's 2022 pact. Germany is taking seriously reports Russia may launch a nuclear-capable satellite before year-end.
Indonesia's Prabowo held talks with MSCI (brokered by Ray Dalio) to avoid a downgrade of Indonesia's market classification.
note: Inference: watch for MSCI index-review outcomes affecting Southeast Asian flows.

item: Tajikistan began withdrawing from the ICC. Arson attacks on ~100 Grameen Bank branches in Bangladesh. Armed drones hit a police HQ in Cucuta, Colombia.
A US federal jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 criminal counts (fraud, sanctions evasion, IP theft) but rejected the racketeering charges; sentencing late next year, Huawei will appeal (Bloomberg).
note: Inference: adds legal backing to the hawks' push for tighter chip controls (Cotton bill) despite the White House's softer line on NVIDIA.

item: Australia's inflation reading came in at 4.9%, nearly double the RBA's target.
note: Inference: another developed-market inflation surprise; supports the 'higher for longer' leg of H2 alongside US CPI and JGB yields.

item: Spain holds a snap general election on Sunday Nov 29; polls favour the conservative PP, possibly in coalition with hard-right Vox.
note: Inference: part of the 2027-28 populist wave the newsletter flagged with France and the ECB.

item: Solomon Islands signed a security treaty with Australia barring foreign military bases, scrapping its 2022 pact with China; Australia offers US$677m in support.
Shanghai Party chief and Politburo member Chen Jining is under investigation, the fourth Politburo member ousted since 2025, ahead of Xi's party congress next year.

UN Secretary-General race is the longest deadlock in UN history; every candidate faces at least two possible P5 vetoes with 36 days left. Europe's 2026 summer heat caused ~50,000 excess deaths (UK research).
